title: CI / Eval GPU Sandbox Onboarding and Promote Playbook
author: Priya Raman
content:
Summary:

This playbook describes a prescriptive, repeatable process for onboarding new evaluation and CI workloads into Redwood's ephemeral GPU sandbox environment, promoting a validated workload into the shared burst/burstable GPU pool, and the associated Terraform/IaC, CI pipeline patterns, and guardrails required to keep cost and capacity within SLOs. It is targeted at infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners who manage GPU-backed CI/eval runners.

Goals:
- Provide a safe, reproducible onboarding flow for teams bringing large eval or CI GPU jobs.
- Enforce IaC-backed sandbox provisioning with network isolation, egress controls, and per-tenant cost caps.
- Define promotion criteria and an automated promote workflow that binds into Terraform module versions and pipeline gating.
- Offer runbook steps for rapid rollback and emergency quarantine.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: ephemeral playground sandboxes, per-team burstable GPU pools, CI/eval pipelines, IaC modules for sandbox tenant lifecycle, cost quota enforcement.
- Non-goals: full Dedicated customer onboarding (see eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity for dedicated flows), on-prem packaging, or workload-specific model tuning.

Prerequisites:
1) Team has a valid Redwood account and infra owner assigned.
2) Team lead has completed the GPU safety and cost training course.
3) An owning GitHub org and CI project are configured to use Redwood’s ephemeral runner images.
4) The team has created a Terraform workspace in the shared infra repo or is authorized to use the self-service module registry.

High-level workflow (steps):
1) Request a sandbox: create a repo issue using the "Sandbox Onboard" template. Include expected concurrency, max GPU type (e.g. a100-80GB), and daily token/compute estimate.
2) Provision via IaC: use the `sandbox-tenant` Terraform module (see example below) in a branch. The module creates a namespaced VPC level NetworkPolicy, IAM role, quota object, and a short-lived service-account token for CI runners.
3) Smoke and stability tests: run a small battery of CI jobs that exercise batching (1–8 sequence lengths), KV cache reuse, and 30-minute long-run stability test.
4) Cost and telemetry verification: validate the tenant's per-job token accounting and per-run latency traces in the cost dashboard.
5) Promote to burst pool: once acceptance criteria are met, open a PR to the infra-promote pipeline that updates the `burst-pool-assignments` module binding and triggers the promote job.

Promotion acceptance criteria (must all pass):
- Performance: p95 latency under 300ms for short gen workloads (<=64 tokens) and stable throughput at requested concurrency for 60-minute run.
- Cost: measured per-token cost within 25% of the estimate used for quota.
- Stability: no memory OOMs, <0.1% GPU preemptions observed during validation runs.
- Security: network isolation confirmed, no public egress observed in packet captures.
- Observability: traces and logs captured with the standard tenant labels, and the cost export to billing bucket is present.

Terraform / IaC patterns:
- Module used: `modules/sandbox-tenant` (inputs summarized below). Teams must not fork the module; instead create a module binding in their infra branch and request review from infra-platform.

Module input table:
| Input name | Type | Default | Notes |
| tenant_name | string | <required> | unique across sandboxes, used in VPC CIDR allocation hint |
| max_gpu_type | string | "a100-40gb" | validated in policy; infra will restrict a100-80gb to approved teams |
| daily_quota_cost_usd | number | 50 | soft enforced via billing alarms |
| egress_policy | string | "restricted" | "open" | "private-link" as allowed values |

Example Terraform snippet:
```hcl
module "sandbox_tenant_teamfoo" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-infra/modules//sandbox-tenant"
  tenant_name = "team-foo-eval-2025"
  max_gpu_type = "a100-40gb"
  daily_quota_cost_usd = 100
  egress_policy = "private-link"
}
```

CI/CD pipeline pattern (GitHub Actions / Tekton example):
- Branch flow: all IaC provisioning must be done in a branch with the module binding and a PR tagged `sandbox-onboard`.
- Pipeline steps (abstracted):
  1. terraform fmt & validate
  2. plan with `-var-file=overrides.tfvars` and upload plan artifact
  3. run static checks (policy-as-code) — reject if module inputs violate allowlist (e.g., request for a100-80gb without reviewer)
  4. apply to sandbox workspace (manual approval for first apply; subsequent updates can be auto-approved)
  5. trigger post-provision smoke job that runs on provisioned runner and reports status to PR

YAML snippet (GitHub Actions simplified):
```yaml
name: Sandbox Onboard
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  terraform: 
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
      - name: Terraform validate
        run: terraform validate
      - name: Policy check
        run: /usr/local/bin/policy-check --input plan.json
      - name: Apply (manual approval)
        if: github.event.pull_request.labels.* contains 'sandbox-onboard'
        run: terraform apply -auto-approve
```

Cost and capacity guardrails:
- Hard quotas: module creates a quota object enforced by the charging service; once daily_quota_cost_usd is exceeded, further jobs are rejected until the next day.
- Soft alarms: infra creates a PagerDuty alert at 80% quota burn and an Opsgenie note for 95% burn.
- Preemption policy: workloads in sandbox are allowed to be preempted for Dedicated SLA traffic. The promote process requires tests that show preemption behavior is tolerable for the workload or that checkpointing exists.

Operational runbook: emergency quarantine and rollback
1. Detection: if alerts indicate runaway cost or repeated OOMs, open an incident with severity P1 if cost burn > 200% expected.
2. Quarantine steps:
   a. Use the infra console to toggle `egress_policy=restricted` for the tenant.
   b. Suspend the tenant's CI runner auth tokens (terraform apply with `suspend=true`).
   c. If network traffic is suspicious, create a VPC flow log snapshot and hand to Security for analysis.
3. Rollback promotion: revert the `burst-pool-assignments` change in the promote PR and re-run the promote pipeline to apply the old binding.
4. Post-incident: require a remediation PR that includes either a lowered quota, improved CI job checkpointing, or a plan for dedicated capacity.

Observability requirements (must be visible before promotion):
- Metrics: per-tenant GPU-hours, token_count, p50/p95 latency, job_failure_rate.
- Logs: model-runtime stderr/stdout capture, kernel OOM summaries, driver errors.
- Traces: end-to-end request traces with tenant_tag and job_id.
- Dashboards: ephemeral-sandbox-perf (team-scoped) and infra-sandbox-overview (global).

Ownership and escalation:
- Requester (team): maintains CI and workload tests, and writes the `onboard` PR.
- Infra Platform: reviews IaC, approves initial apply, creates promote PRs.
- SRE (GPU SRE): validates performance logs and approves promotion.
- Security: reviews network policies for private-link/egress attachments.
- Escalation path: SRE -> Infra Platform -> Eng Director if unresolved after 16 hours.

Related pages and modules:
- modules/sandbox-tenant: implementation reference (internal registry link)
- eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/ephemeral-gpu-pools-for-ci-and-eval-runs.json (operational patterns and image artifacts)
- eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/on-demand-sandbox-gpu-module-with-egress-fencing.json (module lifecycle and constraints)

Appendix A: Example terraform outputs and required secrets:
| Output name | Description | Secret? |
| runner_sa_token | short-lived runner token (expiry 6 hours) | yes |
| tenant_quota_id | quota object id for billing | no |

Appendix B: Sample validation checklist (to attach to PR):
1. IaC plan validated and peer-reviewed.
2. Policy-as-code checks passed.
3. Post-provision smoke job passed (link to CI run).
4. Cost sample: 3 test runs with cost measurements included.
5. Observability: dashboards populated and link provided.
6. Promotion PR created and assigned to GPU SRE for sign-off.
